title: Regional traffic smoothing for streamed session handoffs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: implement an active-active regional traffic smoothing and session-handoff mechanism for the hosted API edge that preserves low tail latency for streaming sessions while enabling rapid cross-region mitigation under partial outages. Context: recent incidents showed abrupt single-region drains cause 95th/99th latency spikes for streaming clients and lose ephemeral session state for long-lived streams. This ticket designs and ships a conservative rollout that introduces a ‘traffic smoothing window’ and session-preservation handshake between gateways, integrates a smart circuit-breaker that favors stream continuity over instantaneous load redistribution, and provides observability + runbook for SREs. Success metrics: reduce 95th latency spikes during regional evacuations by >=40%, reduce stream resets during failover by >=70%, and keep overall request error rate impact to customers to <0.5% during orchestrated switchovers.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway can perform coordinated traffic shift across 2+ regions with a configurable smoothing window (default 45s)
Streaming sessions use a two-phase handshake to transfer in-flight KV/offsets; session continuity verified by synthetic clients
Circuit-breaker will throttle new non-streaming requests before draining streams when region saturates
Automated rollback if tail latency or error-rate exceed safety thresholds during rollout
Dashboards show region pair-level SLOs and a new metric for 'session-handoff success rate' > 95% in integration tests

Circuit breakers: extend existing RB to prefer stream-preservation; add safeguards for CPU/GPU overload (owner: Deniz Ozturk)
E2E tests: build synthetic streamer harness to validate continuity and latency under partial region outage (owner: QE team)
Observability: dashboards, alerts, and tracing tags; integrate with cost telemetry to detect excessive cross-region egress (owner: Observability)
Runbook: author step-by-step failover and rollback instructions for SREs; rehearse in staging and one canary customer (owner: SRE)
Rollout: feature flag gating, canary on one region pair, and graduated ramp to global (owner: Release Engineering)

design_decisions: Prefer handshake-based session transfer over full state replication to limit cross-region bandwidth
Smoothing window default set to 45s after trade-off analysis between client-visible time-to-switch and backend capacity ramping
Circuit-breaker will demote new requests rather than preemptively terminating streams to minimize customer-visible resets
Use feature-flag gating for both smoothing controller and handshake; default off for existing customers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: cross-region KV transfer increases egress costs - Mitigation: TTL and delta-only transfer; cost telemetry and budget alerting
Risk: handshake adds extra latency to cold session handoffs - Mitigation: fall back to probabilistic draining after timeout; monitor client error rates
Risk: routing flaps can invalidate handoff tokens - Mitigation: add token replay window and idempotency on commit
Risk: rollout interacts with existing autoscaling - Mitigation: integrate smoothing controller signals with autoscaler and throttle ramping
qa_plan: Unit tests for handshake edge cases (token expiry, partial commit)
Integration: staged drain in staging with synthetic streamer at 100 rps for 30m
Chaos: introduce region packet loss and verify rollbacks trigger correctly
Canary: run with single enterprise customer behind SLA for 48h
